title: Ciphertext Shortening for Non-Tag-Based Committing AE
summary: The target commitment overhead is at most the parameter s, and SC reduces it further for tag-based schemes; for non-tag-based schemes, impossibility or an SC analogue remains open.

formal_statement.body: For a committing transform applied to a non-tag-based authenticated-encryption scheme, let $\operatorname{co}(s)$ denote the transformed ciphertext length minus the base-scheme ciphertext length; this overhead is a constant depending only on $s$, with target $\operatorname{co}(s)\le s$. For tag-based schemes, the ciphertext-shortening SC transform can reduce this overhead further, but no analogous method or impossibility proof is known for non-tag-based schemes. Determine whether reducing $\operatorname{co}(s)$ further than the $\operatorname{co}(s)\le s$ target is impossible in the non-tag-based setting, or construct an analogue of SC that achieves such a reduction.

scope.domain: Ciphertext-overhead reduction for committing transforms of non-tag-based authenticated-encryption schemes.
parameters: s: parameter on which the constant ciphertext overhead depends and that determines the target upper bound
co(s): transformed ciphertext length minus the base-scheme ciphertext length
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove that reducing the overhead further than the co(s) at most s target is impossible for non-tag-based schemes, or construct an SC analogue that achieves such a reduction.

citations.label: A Universal Transform for Committing Authenticated Encryption

progress.summary: The source sets co(s) at most s as the target and notes that SC can lower the overhead further for tag-based schemes. It says no analogous non-tag-based method or impossibility proof is known.
